subject: Private Stack: Terraform + Helm + Ansible preflight for on-prem VPC
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme-logistics.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bryan Lewis <bryan.lewis@infra-partners.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: IaC preflight for on-prem VPC bundle

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the runbook walkthrough last week. Our security and infra teams want a quick preflight on the Terraform modules, Helm charts, and Ansible tasks before we sign off on the private deployment.

Deliverables we'd appreciate you/checklist to confirm:
- Terraform module layout and module boundary (VPC, subnets, routing, peering)
- tfstate handling + KMS/lock strategy
- Helm chart values and image provenance (policy for private registry)
- Ansible playbook idempotency and user account handling
- CI gate: plan/apply separation, plan output review, who can approve apply
- Network security: NACLs/SGs, required BGP/MPLS hints for our colo, and any default open ports

I attached an exported tfplan and our current helm values sample. Can you confirm what you need from us (secrets, network diagrams, any test harness)? Ideally get this done before EOD Wed so our compliance folks can start the check.

Thanks,
Alice Zhang
Head of Cloud Platforms
Acme Logistics

Attachments: acme-vpc-helm-review.zip (helm values, snippets), tf-plan-output.txt
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: IaC preflight for on-prem VPC bundle

Alice — thanks for the clear list. We can run a lightweight preflight and a deeper pass focusing on state/KMS, CI gating and network adjacency. Proposed scope:

1) Quick review (today–tomorrow)
   - Terraform: module boundaries, naming of outputs/inputs, backend config (S3-like or on-premet K/V), and plan drift indicators
   - Helm: imagePullSecrets, reproducible image tags, and chart hooks that run privileged jobs
   - Ansible: playbook idempotency and vault usage

2) Security checklist (Wed)
   - KMS integration pattern, RBAC for apply jobs, audit log locations
   - Network: confirm CIDR allocations, route tables, firewall policies, and any colo-specific BGP setup

3) Deliverables
   - Quick findings (bullet list) + recommended remediations
   - PR templates and CI updates (GH Actions / Jenkins snippets)

We need read-only access to the repo (link or a PR) and a sanitized tfstate or plan (you attached the plan which is helpful). If you can drop a short network diagram (PNG/PDF) in the Drive link you provided, that will speed up the adjacency check.

I'll kick this off and loop Dev and Laura for deeper reviews on Terraform and Helm respectively. If that timeline looks ok, I'll send a meeting invite for a 30m sync tomorrow afternoon to go over any blocking items.

—Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Initial: IaC preflight for on-prem VPC bundle

Forwarding Alice's plan. Quick notes from my initial pass:

- Terraform: the modules are fine overall but their networking module mixes subnet creation and service endpoints (recommend split: vpc-network module + vpc-services). This makes lifecycle tricky when teams update services.
- Backend: they are using an internal minio-backed state. Need locking (consul/etcd or Dynamo-style lock). No KMS config in the backend block — must confirm how state is encrypted at rest.
- Security groups: I see broad 0.0.0.0/0 on app-egress for health checks. Should be scoped to colo addresses/peers.
- Helm: helm templates include a post-install job that uses hostNetwork: true; we need to confirm justification.

I added inline comments at PR: https://github.com/acme-ops/private-deploy/pull/52 — please take a look and mark items as "blocking" if they need to be fixed before apply.

Also tagging Hiro for the on-prem runtime routing (BGP/MPLS) checklist.

—Dev
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: IaC preflight for on-prem VPC bundle

Thanks — I've reviewed the Helm snippets in the attachment. Specifics I called out in the GH PR:

- imagePullPolicy: If they are tagging with latest for internal builds, we need an image promotion workflow. Recommend image tags be immutable (sha256) and a simple promotion stage in CI.
- charts should not contain secret values; use sealed-secrets or reference a vault at deploy time.
- chart values contain a 'privileged: true' flag on a sidecar container — request rationale.

CI gating: their current GH Action runs terraform plan and auto-comments the plan, but the apply is controlled by a Jenkins job that reads a credentials token. Suggest we:
  - Move apply approvals behind GitHub protected environment approvals OR
  - Ensure Jenkins has MFA and uses a 2-person approval for production applies

I've attached a sanitized ansible-playbook.yml with recommended changes for idempotency and vault usage.

Laura Bennett
Staff DevOps Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ansible-playbook.yml
From: Bryan Lewis <bryan.lewis@infra-partners.io>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: IaC preflight for on-prem VPC bundle

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups from our side after reviewing your comments and the PR: 

- We'll split the networking module as suggested and open a follow-up PR today.
- For state locking, we can enable Consul we manage in the colo; will include a lock table and KMS integration to encrypt the state at rest. We'll drop the new backend config in a PR and request your review.
- The hostNetwork job was an artifact of an older monitoring collector; we'll convert it to a DaemonSet with proper ServiceAccount and remove hostNetwork.
- CI: we can move prod applies to a GitHub protected environment and enable required reviewers for apply.

Next step: Bryan will push the two PRs (network split + backend changes) and assign Dev for the Terraform review and Laura for Helm/CI. We can do a quick 30m sync if any item remains blocked.

Thanks — Bryan
Bryan Lewis
Infra Partner, Infra Partners LLC

Attachment: acme-vpc-helm-review.zip (updated helm values), tf-plan-output.txt (sanitized)
